title: Measure the copy each panel surface declares and where it declares none
question: which sentences does each panel surface declare for itself, at which path:line, which does it render from a literal nobody keeps in a map, and which surface declares none at all?
head: cfdff38990b7715e38a917976dad957b64840cd5
measuredAt: static: all nineteen apps/angular-ai-devtools/src/app/panel-*.ts surfaces (the two *.spec.ts files are named in `excluded`) were read line by line at the head above, every non-comment line carrying a string literal was extracted with a throwaway script that prints `file:line|trimmed line` (kept in the session scratchpad and not checked in), and every citation below was re-read from the file when this record was written. No browser was opened, no page was read, no build and no test of the app was run; the only command executed against these files was that extraction and the verify suite named in `verify`, which re-reads all of them.
lineTextConvention: every `lineText` is the cited line with its leading and trailing whitespace trimmed and nothing else removed, so a line that is a bare string literal carries its quotes and its trailing comma. `line` is 1-indexed. The suite re-reads each cited line and requires it to equal `lineText` exactly and to contain the sentence the record quotes.
scope: Recorded per surface: (a) every sentence it declares in a map or a module constant, with the key it is declared under; (b) every sentence — fixed or interpolated — written inside a function body or a component template instead of being declared; (c) the label prefix of every line the surface builds from a label and a value, because that prefix is copy the surface writes; (d) the multi-word prose fragment a surface substitutes for a value it does not have.

Not enumerated as entries: single-token value words a surface derives into a line (`true`/`false` in panel-navigation.ts:186, `disabled`/`unknown` in panel-fields.ts:232 and :235, `valid`/`invalid` in panel-fields.ts:142). They are named in the surface’s own `notes`, and they are values of a line rather than sentences.

Not recorded at all: the `Error` messages `sentenceText` throws for an id the registry does not carry (panel-components.ts:170, panel-console.ts:268, panel-copy-to-agent.ts:159). They are developer-facing throws and are never rendered to a reader.

notes: The demo host declares its own two template lines inside the component’s `template` string (:447, :448) and its one error sentence by string concatenation (:491). Nothing it writes is in a constant or a map.
It is recorded because it is a `panel-*.ts` file and it renders copy of its own; it is not one of the eighteen subject surfaces, and the lines it renders for them are theirs.
The template also renders `{{ block.state }}` (:456) and `{{ line }}` (:458, :464), which are values with no pane text of their own.

absence.statement: panel-context.ts renders nothing and declares no sentence: it is the adapter that turns the panel’s signals into one `PanelContext`, and its whole surface is three exported types and one pure function.
absence.why: The only string literals in the file’s code are the members of two union types (`outstanding`/`answered`/`failed` and `zone`/`noop`/`unknown`) and the object keys it writes: no template literal, no quoted string containing a space, and no map. Its doc comments are prose and are never rendered. The scan that says so is the suite’s own — scripts/copy-check.test.mjs, the test named "a surface that declares no sentences is recorded as an absence, not skipped" — which strips the comments and then requires zero template literals and zero string literals containing whitespace, with panel-components.ts beside it as the control where the same scan finds nine sentence literals.
absence.consequence: The join in T002 has to answer `cannot-tell` for this surface rather than an empty list, and the record states the absence so that answer is read off a measurement rather than inferred from a missing entry.

notCaptured: No page text was read and no browser was opened for this record. The roadmap’s own observable — the strings a page renders — is not measured here and does not exist in this repository: `innerText` and `textContent` occur 0 times in extension/agent-main.js, counted by the command in `measurements`. Nothing in this record is a reading of a served page.

The record does not measure what a surface renders at runtime. It records the literals the source declares, and a rendered line is those literals joined with values the answer carried; which fields a join supplies, and what a pane does with an absent one, is T002’s join and not this record.

The record does not claim to be exhaustive about single-token value words (see `scope`), and it does not read the baseline stylesheet, the routes table or the demo’s sample facts. `panel-demo.ts` is recorded only for the copy it writes itself.

The record does not judge the copy. It does not claim a sentence is accurate, consistent with its siblings, or supported by the record the pane was handed; it states where each sentence is and what it says, and the three surfaces whose wording the record singles out (panel-navigation.ts:283, panel-sanitizer.ts:180, panel-fields.ts:196) are described and not graded.
No test of the app was run and no build was made. The verify command below runs this record’s own suite and prettier, and nothing else was executed.

verdict: measured: this repository has 19 panel-*.ts surfaces (two more files match the glob and are vitest specs, named in `excluded`). 6 declare their sentences in a map, 11 in loose module constants, 1 only inside a component template and a function, and 1 — panel-context.ts, the signal-to-context adapter — declares no sentence at all because it renders nothing. 79 sentences are declared in a map or a constant, 34 more are written inline where no map can reach them, and 111 label prefixes and 7 prose words are built into lines inline. The roadmap’s premise does not survive the reading: no surface compares anything against a copy digest, and of the 90 sentences this record carries exactly 1 occurs in either digest the repository ships (extension/error-digest.json, extension/image-digest.json) — the one hit is the single word `available` (error-boundary/RESET_TEXT), which occurs in a digest body and explains no rendered line. What exists is the copy measured here, and the digest T002 authors will be the first one that holds it.
